attribution.note: Joint post that Marcus co-wrote and published on his own Substack. He commits to the bet in his own name.

semantics.note: Taking one side of a wager is an unhedged commitment, like 'I bet', so it counts as a forecast. The proposition keeps the bet's terms: the panel decides, feasibility counts, there are tailoring limits, and physical tasks are excluded. It also keeps the odds disclaimer.

contract.note: The contract defers to the panel the two sides agreed on and treats the cost figures as examples. Both choices match what the bet itself says. Its early-resolution rule only allows an early contradiction, which is fair.

evidence.note: This is the original post. It sets out how the bet will be judged but contains no evidence about the outcome.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2027-12-31, after the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. No panel ruling was found, and no final early ruling certifying 8 or more tasks exists. The forecast is not due, so it stays unresolved.
